name: TX-33
label: Safe D

key_factors: Colin Allred's large fundraising advantage and name recognition
Open seat after Crockett's retirement, but seat stays with Democrats
model.rationale: TX-33's D+18 partisan lean makes this a heavily Democratic seat even without Crockett on the ballot, and Allred's $7.4 million raised dwarfs any visible Republican effort. Markets price Democrats around 96%, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: A late surge of outside Republican spending or an unexpectedly strong Gillespie campaign could narrow the margin, though a flip remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jasmine Crockett (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
TX-33 is a heavily Democratic Dallas-area seat with an 18-point Democratic partisan lean. Incumbent Jasmine Crockett is retiring to run for Senate, leaving an open seat, but the district's fundamentals strongly favor Democrats. Former Rep. Colin Allred, the Democratic nominee, has raised over $7.4 million and brings statewide name recognition from his 2024 Senate run, while Republican Patrick Gillespie has shown little visible fundraising or outside support.

Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 96%, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. The forecast expects Democrats to hold the seat comfortably, with the main uncertainty being the size of the margin rather than the winner.
